title: AI
description: Extract structured data from each input row using an AI model. Define the desired fields with output, or reuse a saved definition with model_id.

parameters.name: api_key
parameters.description: OpenAI API key used for this wrangle, normally supplied through a recipe variable.

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: Input column name, column index, or list of columns supplied together as DATA for each row. If omitted, all dataframe columns are supplied.

parameters.name: output
parameters.description: Desired extraction. Use an object keyed by output column name for structured fields, a string for one prompted value, or an array of field names/definitions. Each field may use the schema options below.

type.description: JSON data type required for this field. If omitted, common scalar types are accepted. Fields allow null by default.

parameters.name: model_id
parameters.description: ID of a saved extract.ai definition. Use it instead of defining an output schema. When output is also supplied with model_id in a recipe, output names the destination column or columns for the saved fields.

parameters.name: record_examples
parameters.description: Whole-record examples. Each example has a separate input value or record and the complete expected output record. Optional name and notes provide model-visible context. Use {name: ..., notes: ..., input: ..., output: ...}. Omitted nullable output fields are completed with null. Required non-null nested properties must be supplied. This differs from examples nested under one output field, which teach only that field.

parameters.name: output_format
parameters.description: How extracted fields are written. columns writes one dataframe column per field (default); dictionary keeps one object; concatenate joins fields into one string using char.

parameters.name: char
parameters.description: Separator used only when output_format is concatenate. Defaults to comma-space.

parameters.name: web_search
parameters.description: Enable OpenAI Responses web search; the model decides when searching helps. When true, every row also receives web_search_sources: a deduplicated list of {title, url} objects in source order, or an empty list when no source was used. This reserved column is automatic. Requires protocol responses. Defaults to false.

parameters.name: instructions
parameters.description: Additional guidance applied to every input row. Use this for decision rules, evidence priorities, normalization requirements, or other behavior that applies to the complete extraction.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: OpenAI model ID for this call. If omitted, uses the configured extract.ai default; a saved model definition may supply its own model.

parameters.name: threads
parameters.description: Maximum number of row-level requests sent in parallel. The configured default is 32.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Maximum seconds for one HTTP attempt. The configured default is 12; deadline can end the overall call sooner.

parameters.name: retries
parameters.description: Number of additional attempts after a retryable failure. The configured default is 1. Backoff and request timeouts remain bounded by deadline.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Override the endpoint for the selected protocol. A chat/completions URL selects the legacy protocol only when protocol is omitted; new recipes should use the configured Responses endpoint.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: AI service provider. Currently only OpenAI is supported.

parameters.name: protocol
parameters.description: OpenAI API protocol. Responses is the configured default and is required for web_search; chat_completions remains available for legacy definitions.

parameters.name: deadline
parameters.description: Total seconds allowed for the entire wrangle call, including queued work, retries, and backoff. The configured default is 15.

parameters.name: store
parameters.description: Whether OpenAI may store Responses API results. Defaults to false.

parameters.name: cache
parameters.description: Reuse identical successful results from the bounded warm-instance cache. Defaults to true. Set false when fresh model or web results are required.

parameters.name: cache_ttl
parameters.description: Maximum age in seconds for a cached result used by this call. Applies to extracted values and web_search_sources together.

parameters.name: strict
parameters.description: Require OpenAI structured-output strict mode. Defaults to true. Definitions with dynamic dictionary keys automatically switch to non-strict provider mode and are still validated locally.

parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: Responses API reasoning controls. Set effort for reasoning-capable models. The configured default is none when that model supports it; otherwise the provider default applies.

parameters.name: verbosity
parameters.description: Responses API text verbosity for compatible models. Defaults to low when supported; ignored with a warning for incompatible models.

parameters.name: if
parameters.description: Condition that determines whether the wrangle runs as a whole. Recipe variables may be referenced with `${variable}`.

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: Filter rows before applying the wrangle using SQL-like criteria, such as `column1 = 123 OR column2 = 'abc'`.

parameters.name: where_params
parameters.description: Values used with `where` for parameterized criteria. Uses SQLite placeholder syntax such as `?` or `:name`.

guidance:
Use AI to extract meaningful structured data. `extract.ai` can be used recipe-first, where the output schema is defined in the recipe, or model-first, where a saved extract.ai model is called by `model_id`. :::info For saved extract.ai models, this is the preferred calling pattern compared with using `extract.custom`. ::: ## Migrated examples #### Making Use of Output Parameters ##### Recipe ```yaml wrangles: - extract.ai: api_key: Your OpenAI api key input: Product Specs output: Blade Diameter: type: number description: The diameter of the blade used, reported in inches. default: N/A examples: - 4.5" - 8 inch Max. RPM: type: number description: The maximum rotations per minute (rpm). default: 3600 examples: - 3600 max. rpm ```
##### Input Sample | Product Specs | | --- | | 18V Cordless 4.5in angle grinder | | 120V 12in chop saw 3600 max. rpm |
##### Output Sample | Blade Diameter | Max. RPM | | --- | --- | | 4.5 inches | | | 12 inches | 3600 |
#### Description Only ##### Recipe ```yaml wrangles: - extract.ai: api_key: Your OpenAI api key input: Product Specs output: Blade Diameter: The diameter of the blade used, reported in inches. Max. RPM: The maximum rotations per minute (rpm). ```
##### Input Sample | Product Specs | | --- | | 18V Cordless 4.5in angle grinder | | 120V 12in chop saw 3600 max. rpm |
##### Output Sample | Blade Diameter | Max. RPM | | --- | --- | | 4.5 inches | | | 12 inches | 3600 |
#### Model Based Column Output by Name ##### Recipe ```yaml wrangles: - extract.ai: api_key: Your OpenAI api key model_id: xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxx output: - Colors - Sizes ```
##### Input Sample | Items | | --- | | Large yellow square | | Medium orange triangle |
##### Output Sample | Colors | Sizes | | --- | --- | | [yellow] | Large | | [orange] | Medium |
